chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a jar in which a beetle was found that had died. He said: “Throw it out and perform wudu (ablution) from it; but if it was a scorpion, then pour out the water and perform wudu (ablution) from other water.” And about a man who has two vessels containing water, and filth fell into one of them but he does not know which of the two it is, and he is not able to obtain other water, he said: “He pours them both out and performs tayammum.”

key_terms.جَرَّةٍ: a jar or large vessel containing water
key_terms.خُنْفَسَاءُ: a beetle found dead in the water
key_terms.عَقْرَبًا: a scorpion, whose presence changes the ruling on the water
key_terms.قَذَرٌ: filth or impurity that falls into one of the vessels
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum instead of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should be done if an insect or impurity falls into water used for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on taharah (ritual purity) and the use of water for wudu (ablution). It distinguishes between different creatures falling into water and also rules that when impurity affects one of two water containers indistinguishably, both are discarded and tayammum is performed if no other water is available.
